title: RubRIX: Rubric-Driven Risk Mitigation in Caregiver-AI Interactions

bias_targets.methodology: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation of model responses to caregiver queries using the RubRIX framework's binary audit questions to detect infantilizing language, dehumanizing descriptions, and ableist framing of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) symptoms.
LLM-as-a-judge evaluation of model responses to identify stigmatizing language, victim-blaming, assumptions of moral failings, and martyrdom expectations directed at informal caregivers.

LLM-as-a-judge evaluation of model responses to detect gendered role expectations and assumptions about caregiving duties (e.g., assuming caregivers are always women or framing caregiving as a maternal duty).
LLM-as-a-judge evaluation of model responses to identify ethnocentric recommendations, assumptions of Western family structures, and ignorance of cultural or religious care practices.
LLM-as-a-judge evaluation of model responses to detect ageist assumptions about capability, value, or needs, as well as patronizing language directed toward older adults and care recipients.
